jobs.description:
Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

At EA, we believe games are powerful because they bring together multiple ways people engage: play, watch, create, and connect. And increasingly, the biggest entertainment platforms aren't just places to consume content - they're places where communities build.

Creator-made content is already a proven part of EA's history - from community creation tools in Battlefield to The Gallery in The Sims 4. We believe new creative technologies and tools will expand how players engage with and contribute to our experiences, supported by thoughtful product design, safety systems, and global reach. Our focus is on enabling more players to participate in creative expression by making creation easier, safer, and more rewarding.

As a Technical Director, you will lead the technical strategy for capturing research data from EA game sources. You will define how dedicated title streams, shared instrumentation, capture builds, and downstream data systems work together as a unified capability for Research & Engineering.

You will be responsible for driving the architecture, standards, priorities, and technical outcomes of the Game Data Capture team. You will coordinate across researchers, ML Data Engineers, title teams, central infrastructure, security, and legal partners while remaining hands-on in the most consequential technical decisions.

This is a hybrid role, working three days per week in Redwood City, Montreal, or Vancouver.

You will report to the Lead Technical Director.

Responsibilities

You will define the technical vision, architecture, and roadmap for a unified cross-title game-data capture capability.
You will establish standards for supported modalities, synchronization, coordinate systems, schemas, build identity, provenance, validation, and platform performance.
You will determine which capabilities belong in the shared capture platform and which require title-specific integration.
You will prioritize title onboarding and research requests based on technical feasibility, research value, dependencies, and long-term platform leverage.
You will lead architecture and design reviews for capture SDKs, title adapters, build automation, and interfaces with central data infrastructure.
You will partner with title technical leaders to secure the expertise, access, and production safeguards needed to instrument complex game codebases.
You will define requirements for dedicated Perforce streams, automated merges, reproducible builds, CI/CD, deployment, and capture validation.
You will establish clear technical acceptance criteria for certified raw capture sessions and ensure limitations are documented.
You will identify repeated title-specific needs and guide the team toward maintainable shared solutions.
You will mentor engineers, communicate technical direction, resolve cross-team decisions, and represent Game Data Capture to research and technology leadership.

Qualifications

12+ years of professional software engineering experience, including technical leadership in AAA games, game engines, real-time simulation, or related systems
Experience setting architecture and technical direction across multiple engineering teams or products
Expertise in C++ and strong working knowledge of large, multithreaded game-engine codebases
Broad experience with engine systems such as rendering, simulation, gameplay, animation, physics, audio, tools, or build pipelines
Experience integrating technology across actively developed branches, platforms, or title codebases
Experience with Perforce, complex build systems, CI/CD, and release or integration workflows
Experience translating research or product requirements into platform strategy and executable technical plans
Experience balancing rapid experimentation with security, performance, stability, maintainability, and partner-team constraints

From leadership that brings out your potential, to creating space for learning and experimenting, we empower you to do great work and pursue opportunities for growth.

Our packages are tailored to meet local needs and may include healthcare coverage, mental well-being support, retirement savings, paid time off, family leaves, complimentary games, and more. Job Description

On behalf of our public-sector client, Affinity is seeking a Chief Courts Information Officer to be accountable for the strategic leadership, governance, and delivery of information management (IM), information technology (IT), and digital services for the Courts. The CCIO ensures that court information systems, digital services, and technology investments support judicial independence, court administration, access to justice, operational efficiency, privacy, and security.

Responsibilities

Develop and implement information management strategies and polices to ensure the secure and efficient handling of Court information.
Project management, change management and strategic planning processes for the effective delivery and management of both short and long-term information technology goals set by the judiciary.
Represent the interests of the judiciary recognizing judicial independence in their day-today operations of and/or projects involving implementing and/or updating software, databases and digital tools used by the judiciary or involving judicial data and court information.
Must operate with full confidence of the Chief Justices and the Chief Judge, be discreet as required and understand the highly confidential and sensitive nature of the work that they perform.
The Chief Court Information Officer (“CCIO”) must have the ability to work cooperatively and harmoniously with all members of the judiciary and both senior and front-line court administration staff, as we as internal and external stakeholders.
Lead the modernization of court information systems, including case management, e-filing, digital evidence, and courtroom technology.

Qualifications

Education and/or training involving computer science, information technology, cyber security or related field.
Significant work experience, preferably 5 years or more, in information technology and information governance, with a focus on cybersecurity and records retention.
Strong understanding of legal and regulatory requirements related to information management, cybersecurity, and records retention.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective information management strategies for an increasingly digital legal work environment.
Extensive experience conducting IT and information security research and providing advice and opinions, preferably at a senior executive level.
Demonstrated ability to prepare written opinions, memoranda and reports.
The incumbent must have a superior understanding of the principles of judicial independence and possess strong political acumen and experience in the application of discretion and diplomacy to ensure positive outcomes and confidence in the administration of justice.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills in order to accomplish the position’s responsibilities and meet target dates and set priorities.
Experience using MS Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio and Outlook and online legal research databases which may be used by the judiciary. Familiarity with JUDICLOUD (federally appointed judges email network) and/or PowerBI is considered an asset.
Stakeholder engagement - Build effective relationships with the judiciary, court administrators, justice partners, central government IT organizations, and external stakeholders.
Represent the Courts on inter jurisdictional, justice sector, and government technology forums, as required.
Communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
On-site attendance is a mandatory requirement for this role.
Must be able to provide a satisfactory criminal record check and security clearance.
The Resource will be required to execute a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) and maintain strict confidentiality with respect to all information obtained or accessed in the course of performing the Services.
Relevant certifications such as the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
A law degree from an accredited university or college recognized in Manitoba.

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Digital Marketing Director you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

Ontario Plants Propagation (OP) is a leading North American plant propagation company focused on producing high-quality young vegetable and soft fruit plants for commercial greenhouse growers. As a critical supplier to the controlled environment agriculture sector, OP combines horticultural expertise, advanced growing capabilities, and a commitment to innovation to support a more resilient, productive, and sustainable food system.

Following the development of its state-of-the-art Glencoe greenhouse facility and significant capital investment, OP is entering an exciting next phase of growth and transformation. The organization is focused on optimizing operations, enhancing profitability, expanding capabilities, and strengthening its position in a market benefiting from growing demand for greenhouse-grown food production.

The Mandate

Reporting directly to the CEO and working closely with ownership, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will play a central role in helping build a high-performing, scalable, and profitable organization. This is not a traditional finance leadership position focused solely on stewardship and reporting. It is an opportunity to become a true business partner and strategic leader, influencing critical decisions that will shape the future of the company.

The successful candidate will join at a pivotal point in OP's evolution. With substantial investments already made in infrastructure and growth, the organization is seeking a finance leader who can help unlock value by improving profitability, strengthening cash generation, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and building the financial and operational foundations needed to support long-term success.

For an executive who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, building capabilities, and creating lasting impact, this role offers a rare opportunity to influence strategy, strengthen culture, enhance performance, and leave a visible mark on a growing business.

Leadership and Stewardship

The company is seeking a CFO who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. More than just a technical financial leader, the successful candidate will be a thoughtful and credible executive who fosters trust, accountability, and collaboration across the organization and partners effectively with external stakeholders.
Operationally curious and highly intelligent, with a low-ego leadership style
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and complexity
A builder of high-performing teams and organizational culture
Results-oriented and accountable
An enabler of exceptional data-driven decision making
Collaborative, trusted, and relationship-focused
Energized by operational challenges and continuous improvement
An effective and transparent communicator

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will be a strategic and operational finance executive who enjoys complexity and thrives in a growth-oriented environment. They will bring both financial expertise and a passion for helping businesses improve performance and create value.
CPA designation required.
Proven track record of success as a CFO or senior finance executive within a complex operating environment with a minimum of 15 years, including optimizing and scaling organizations
Accomplished as a strategic business partner, advisor to the CEO and the senior leadership team
Hands-on and strategic capabilities in financial planning, forecasting, cash flow management, and business intelligence, driving operational improvements through financial insights and performance management.
Experience operating in asset-intensive, capital-intensive, or leveraged environments.
Track record of building high-performing teams and influencing leaders across an organization.
Experience in manufacturing, food production, agriculture, horticulture, or other operationally intensive industries is strongly preferred.
Experience working with sophisticated lenders, private equity sponsors, family offices, or institutional investors is also an asset.

Location

The CFO will maintain a meaningful on-site presence and build strong relationships across both operating locations. Regular travel between St. Thomas and Glencoe is expected as part of developing a deep understanding of the business and supporting operational excellence.

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to join an organization at a defining moment in its journey. Significant investments have been made, the platform for growth is in place, and the leadership team is focused on realizing the full potential of the business. For a finance executive who wants to influence strategy, strengthen operations, develop teams, and help create long-term enterprise value, this role offers both challenge and impact.
